storage: About 126 MB in PostGIS (measured Oct 11): 108 MB the 21,999 polygons (2.66 M vertices, whole, plus a 5 m simplified copy and indexes), 13 MB the map units with their valley-zoom geometry, the rest components, horizons and the survey areas' boundaries; under 5,000 photo-statistics rows per photo build (about 1 MB), old builds kept. Each photo build's folder ($TVT_ARCHIVE/soils/photo/<build>/: run.json, the windows' sums, stats.json, report.json, calibration.json) is about 80 MB, and its 2 m NAIP COG for the ground 3.4 GB on the cold drive (with about 3 GB of 2 m parts until it's made and checked). Each prepared folder ($TVT_ARCHIVE/soils/prepared/<stamp>/) is about 75 MB, and each export ($TVT_ARCHIVE/soils/export/<build>/) about 47 MB. Reloaded once a year at most.
ethics: USDA NRCS's soil survey: public domain, credited "Soils: USDA NRCS, Soil Survey Geographic Database (SSURGO)". Not for regulatory decisions, as NRCS says, and the card says so. Downloaded by hand with the owner's OK for each yearly refresh; no collector and no schedule. Soils, not people. The photo statistics (soils.photo_stats, soils.ground_colour and the palette) are measured from USDA NAIP 2025 through mask v0, which is built from OpenStreetMap and Overture, so they are ODbL as a whole and credit every input (the naip_photo entry; each build records its own in soils.build); their Sentinel-2 parts (the green rule, the NDVI curves, the colour gains) are Copernicus data, credited.
